title: Double check valve leaking: cover, test cock or housing?
description: Separate external double-check leaks from failed internal checks. Read Watts 007 and Wilkins 350XL drawings, compare repair scope, and prepare the test and retest evidence.
prompt: Is water leaving a test cock, cover, shutoff, check area, or connected pipe?
answer: Double-check leakage must be located before a repair choice is made. The external point of water does not by itself prove an internal check failure, and the exact assembly controls any service kit path.
urgency: Escalate body damage, failed isolation, high-hazard uncertainty, or a leak that cannot be safely contained.
diagramAlt: Conceptual double-check assembly showing two check covers, isolation valves and test ports
identifiers: Identify the assembly by label and nominal size, not the phrase double check.
Record the external leak location and any test result separately.
A change in protection type is an authority decision, not a leak repair choice.

fieldSections.title: An external leak does not prove a failed internal check.
fieldSections.introduction: A double-check assembly has no RPZ relief outlet. If water is leaving a central relief valve, revisit the device identity before selecting a kit.

rows.meaning: The wet point is a test connection; an internal check failure requires a field test.
rows.nextStep: Record the port location. Have a qualified tester inspect it; do not plug it.

fieldSections.introduction: Keep external water, the failed-test reading and the proposed parts as three separate pieces of evidence. These manufacturer examples are not interchangeable kit recommendations.

caseStudies.title: California school, 1995: deteriorated internal seals
caseStudies.constraint: The report describes a nonstandard double-check valve with badly deteriorated rubber gaskets.
caseStudies.documentedAction: EPA’s review, citing Craun and Calderon, records illness associated with drinking water from that system.
caseStudies.planningLesson: A dry exterior does not establish internal protection. This historical summary names no current model and does not document an external leak or a successful repair; it cannot diagnose your assembly.

questions.question: Can a double-check valve fail without leaking outside?
questions.answer: Yes. Internal check sealing and the external pressure boundary are different functions. A dry exterior does not establish a passing field test; preserve the tester’s readings and failed-check identification.

questions.question: Why is water leaking around the cover or housing?
questions.answer: It identifies an external wet boundary, not the exact failed part. The Watts 007 drawing separates a cover O-ring from internal checks; the Wilkins 350XL drawing separates housing O-rings from check components. Confirm the exact model and size before specifying service.

questions.question: Why is water coming from a relief vent on my double check?
questions.answer: Revisit the device identity. A DCVA does not have an RPZ differential relief valve. Photograph the whole device, read its model label and compare the RPZ leak guide before ordering parts.

questions.question: Can I swap the first and second check components?
questions.answer: Do not assume interchangeability. The 007 manual distinguishes first/second seats and springs and names specific M1/M2 exceptions. A generic family name cannot determine fit; have the repairer follow the exact model instructions.

questions.question: Is stopping the external leak enough to close a failed test?
questions.answer: Confirm a passing retest after the relevant maintenance and the governing authority’s report/acceptance requirements. A stopped drip is not a substitute for internal check performance or accepted paperwork.
